CLIENT REQUIREMENTS CHECKLIST
for Notified Body Audits
Regulation (EU) 2023/1542
of the European Parliament and of the Council
of 12 July 2023
concerning batteries and waste batteries
Consolidated version: 02023R1542 — EN — 31.07.2025 — 002.004
Source: EUR-Lex
Contents of this document

This checklist is a practical companion for battery manufacturers, producers and economic operators preparing for Notified Body audits under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. It translates the legal requirements into concrete evidence points that must be prepared, maintained and presented.

Each section contains a short summary based on the Regulation text, followed by a detailed Evidence checklist of the specific proof, documents, samples, calculations, records and system elements expected during an audit.
Key application dates:
Battery Passport (Art. 77): from 18 February 2027 for LMT, industrial >2 kWh and EV batteries
Due diligence obligations (Art. 48 et seq.): from 18 August 2027 for operators with net turnover ≥ EUR 40 million
Carbon footprint declaration (Art. 7): phased from 2025/2026 depending on battery category
Recycled content (Art. 8): declarations from 2028, minimum shares from 2031
Separate collection symbol (Art. 13): from 18 August 2025

Always verify against the latest official consolidated text and any applicable delegated or implementing acts. Annex V safety parameters apply only to stationary battery energy storage systems (SBESS) where the corresponding hazard exists.

1. Manufacturer Obligations (Article 38)

Article 38 sets out the core obligations of manufacturers when placing batteries on the market or putting them into service. Manufacturers must ensure design and manufacture in conformity with the sustainability, safety and information requirements, prepare technical documentation, issue the EU Declaration of Conformity, affix the CE marking, maintain records for 10 years, ensure ongoing conformity of series production, and implement identification and corrective action processes.
1.1 Design & manufacture in conformity

Manufacturers shall ensure that the battery has been designed and manufactured in accordance with Articles 6 to 10 and Articles 12 and 14, and is accompanied by clear, understandable and readable instructions and safety information in the language(s) determined by the Member State of placement.
Evidence checklist:
Design records and risk analysis demonstrating compliance with Art. 6 (hazardous substances), Arts. 9–10 (performance & durability), Art. 12 (stationary storage safety) and Art. 14 (BMS data access)
Instructions for use and safety information available in all required languages of the target Member States
Evidence that the instructions cover normal operation, maintenance, emergency procedures and end-of-life handling
Documented design review and risk assessment process
Traceability of design decisions to applicable requirements
1.2 Marking and labelling
The battery must be marked and labelled in accordance with Article 13 (general information, capacity, separate collection symbol, chemical symbols for Cd/Pb where applicable, and QR code).
Evidence checklist:
Sample labels and packaging specimens showing all required Art. 13 elements
Verification that the separate collection symbol covers at least 3 % of the largest side (or 1.5 % for cylindrical cells), maximum 5 × 5 cm
Where size constraints apply, evidence that symbols are correctly placed on packaging (≥ 1 × 1 cm)
Correct placement and sizing of Cd or Pb chemical symbols beneath the collection symbol where thresholds are exceeded
Label specimens included in the technical documentation
1.3 Technical documentation prepared

Before placement on the market, manufacturers must draw up the technical documentation referred to in Annex VIII and carry out (or have carried out) the relevant conformity assessment procedure under Article 17.
Evidence checklist:
Complete technical file containing all Annex VIII elements
Records of the conformity assessment procedure applied (Module A, D1 or G)
Evidence that the documentation was completed before market placement
Document control and versioning of the technical file
1.4 EU Declaration of Conformity & CE marking
Where compliance has been demonstrated, manufacturers shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity in accordance with Article 18 and affix the CE marking in accordance with Articles 19 and 20.
Evidence checklist:
Signed EU Declaration of Conformity identifying the battery model
Evidence of correct CE marking application (on battery, packaging or accompanying documents)
Where required, the notified body identification number correctly affixed
DoC kept together with the technical documentation for 10 years
1.5 10-year retention

Manufacturers shall keep the technical documentation (Annex VIII) and the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of national authorities for 10 years after the battery has been placed on the market or put into service.
Evidence checklist:
Documented retention procedure and system (electronic and/or paper)
Evidence of secure storage and retrieval capability for the full 10-year period
Access rights, backup and disaster-recovery arrangements
Defined responsibility for long-term document control
1.6 Series production conformity procedures

Manufacturers shall ensure that procedures are in place for batteries that are part of series production to remain in conformity. Changes in production process, design, characteristics, harmonised standards or common specifications must be adequately taken into account.
Evidence checklist:
Documented procedure for ongoing conformity of series production
Change control process covering design, process and standard changes
Records of periodic verification or sampling confirming continued conformity
Impact assessment of changes on declared conformity
1.7 Identification (model / batch / serial)

Batteries must bear a model identification and batch or serial number (or other element) allowing their identification. Where size or nature does not allow it, the information shall be provided on the packaging or accompanying document.
Evidence checklist:
Traceability system linking model, batch and individual serial numbers
Samples showing correct placement of identification on battery or packaging
Records demonstrating unique identification throughout the supply chain
Ability to retrieve design and production data from any identifier
1.8 Corrective action process

Where a manufacturer considers or has reason to believe that a battery is not in conformity, it shall immediately take corrective action to bring it into conformity, withdraw it or recall it. Where the battery presents a risk, the market surveillance authority must be immediately informed.
Evidence checklist:
Documented corrective action, withdrawal and recall procedure
Process for notifying market surveillance authorities in case of risk
Records of past non-conformities and actions taken (if any)
Defined criteria for escalation and authority notification
2. Technical Documentation (Annex VIII)

Annex VIII defines the content of the technical documentation that must enable assessment of conformity with the relevant requirements. The documentation must cover design, manufacture and operation of the battery and include an adequate risk analysis.
2.1 General description & intended use
A general description of the battery and its intended use.
Evidence checklist:
Document describing battery category, chemistry, capacity, voltage, intended application and user
Clear statement of intended use and any restrictions
Identification of relevant battery category (portable, LMT, SLI, industrial, EV, SBESS)
2.2 Design & manufacturing drawings
Conceptual design and manufacturing drawings and schemes of components, sub-assemblies and circuits.
Evidence checklist:
Complete set of design and manufacturing drawings (mechanical, electrical, thermal)
Bills of materials and component specifications
Schematics of circuits, BMS and safety systems
2.3 Explanatory descriptions
Descriptions and explanations necessary for the understanding of the drawings and schemes and the operation of the battery.
Evidence checklist:
Explanatory notes linking drawings to functional descriptions
Description of operating principles and safety features
Explanation of BMS functions and protective measures
2.4 Label specimen
A specimen of the label required in accordance with Article 13.
Evidence checklist:
Physical or high-resolution digital specimen of the Art. 13 label
Verification against Annex VI requirements (Parts A, B and C)
Evidence of correct size, contrast and placement of QR code
2.5 List of standards applied
List of harmonised standards (Art. 15), common specifications (Art. 16) and other technical specifications applied, with indication of which parts have been applied.
Evidence checklist:
Complete list of applied standards and specifications with version numbers
Where standards are only partially applied, clear indication of applied parts
Justification for any alternative solutions adopted
Reference to state-of-the-art testing methodologies used for Annex V
2.6 Calculation & examination results
Results of design calculations made and the examinations carried out, and the technical or documentary evidence used, plus test reports.
Evidence checklist:
Design calculation reports (structural, thermal, electrical, safety)
Examination and test reports from competent laboratories
Supporting technical or documentary evidence
Risk analysis covering applicable hazards
2.7 Carbon footprint study (if applicable)
For batteries subject to Article 7, a study supporting the carbon footprint values and class, containing calculations according to the delegated act methodology and evidence of input data.
Evidence checklist:
Full carbon footprint study per model and manufacturing plant
Calculation worksheets following the Commission methodology
Documented sources and evidence for all input data
Public version of the study available via web link
2.8 Recycled content evidence (if applicable)
For batteries subject to Article 8, a study supporting the recycled content share, containing calculations according to the delegated act methodology and evidence of input data.
Evidence checklist:
Recycled content calculation study per model, year and plant
Mass-balance or equivalent traceability evidence for Co, Pb, Li, Ni
Supplier declarations and supporting documentation
Reconciliation of input materials to declared percentages
3. Conformity Assessment Modules (Annex VIII)

Article 17 and Annex VIII define the applicable conformity assessment modules. Module D1 (quality assurance of the production process) is commonly used for series production and requires an approved quality system subject to notified body surveillance. Module G is used for unit verification. Module A is internal production control.
3.1 Module D1 quality system documentation

The manufacturer must operate an approved quality system for production, final inspection and testing. The quality system documentation must systematically describe quality objectives, organisational structure, processes, controls and records.
Evidence checklist:
Quality manual and procedures covering all elements of Annex VIII Part B point 5.2
Description of organisational structure and responsibilities
Procedures for monitoring carbon footprint and recycled content data
Notified body approval decision of the quality system
Records of quality system changes and notified body evaluation of those changes
3.2 Module D1 on-site readiness
The notified body assessment includes an on-site visit. Production processes, records and personnel must be ready for audit.
Evidence checklist:
Production areas and processes accessible for audit
Current work instructions and process control records available
Qualified personnel available for interviews
Access to inspection, testing and storage sites
Quality records (inspection reports, calibration data, personnel qualification) ready for review
3.3 Module G unit documentation
For batteries not manufactured in series, Module G requires technical documentation and the unit ready for individual verification by a notified body.
Evidence checklist:
Complete technical documentation for the specific unit
Unit available for notified body examination, calculation, measurement and testing
Certificate of conformity issued by the notified body
4. Carbon Footprint (Article 7)

Article 7 requires a carbon footprint declaration for electric vehicle batteries, rechargeable industrial batteries >2 kWh and LMT batteries. The declaration must be calculated per model and manufacturing plant according to the methodology set out in a Commission delegated act, based on Annex II essential elements. Performance classes and maximum thresholds will follow in later stages.
4.1 Carbon footprint declaration

A declaration shall be drawn up for each battery model per manufacturing plant containing administrative information, model information, plant location, carbon footprint (kg CO₂e / kWh), life-cycle stage breakdown, DoC identification and a web link to the public study.
Evidence checklist:
Completed carbon footprint declaration in the format of the implementing act
Public version of the supporting study available via web link
Evidence that the declaration accompanies the battery until accessible via QR code
Administrative information about the manufacturer and battery model
Geographic location of the manufacturing plant
4.2 Calculation methodology evidence
The technical documentation must demonstrate that the carbon footprint and classification have been calculated in accordance with the methodology of the relevant delegated act.
Evidence checklist:
Detailed calculation report following the Commission methodology
Mapping of calculation steps to Annex II essential elements
Verification that the methodology was correctly applied
Evidence of independent review or verification where applicable
4.3 Input data sources
All input data used in the calculation must be documented with sources and evidence.
Evidence checklist:
Documented data sources for energy, materials, transport, processes, etc.
Primary data preferred; secondary data justified and referenced
Traceability of data to supplier declarations or measured values
Data quality assessment and uncertainty evaluation
4.4 Life-cycle stage breakdown
The carbon footprint must be differentiated according to life-cycle stages as described in point 4 of Annex II.
Evidence checklist:
Breakdown by raw material acquisition, manufacturing, distribution, use and end-of-life
Consistency with Annex II modelling requirements
Clear allocation of emissions to each life-cycle stage
5. Recycled Content (Article 8)

Article 8 requires documentation of the percentage share of cobalt, lithium or nickel recovered from manufacturing or post-consumer waste present in active materials, and of lead recovered from waste, for industrial batteries >2 kWh, EV batteries and SLI batteries (LMT from 2033). Minimum percentage shares become mandatory from 2031 (and higher targets from 2036).
5.1 Recycled content declaration
Documentation containing the percentage shares for Co, Li, Ni and Pb (as applicable) must accompany the battery, per model, year and manufacturing plant.
Evidence checklist:
Annual recycled content declaration per model and plant
Format compliant with the Commission delegated act
Clear identification of the battery model and manufacturing plant
Declared percentages for cobalt, lithium, nickel and lead as applicable
5.2 Traceability / mass-balance evidence
The percentages must be supported by supplier documentation, mass-balance systems or equivalent traceability records.
Evidence checklist:
Mass-balance calculations or chain-of-custody documentation
Supplier certificates or declarations of recycled content
Reconciliation of input materials to declared percentages
Evidence distinguishing manufacturing waste from post-consumer waste
5.3 Annual reporting readiness
A system must be in place for annual declarations per model and plant.
Evidence checklist:
Procedure and system for collecting and calculating annual data
Defined responsibilities and timelines for annual reporting
Archive of previous annual declarations
Process for updating declarations when material sources change
6. Battery Due Diligence (Articles 47–53, Annex X)

From 18 August 2027, economic operators with net turnover ≥ EUR 40 million must implement battery due diligence policies covering the raw materials listed in Annex X (cobalt, natural graphite, lithium, nickel and related compounds) and the associated social and environmental risk categories. The system must be verified and periodically audited by a notified body.
6.1 Due diligence policy
Adopt and clearly communicate to suppliers and the public a company battery due diligence policy concerning the Annex X materials and risk categories.
Evidence checklist:
Approved due diligence policy document
Evidence of public communication (website, supplier portal)
Communication records to suppliers
Policy covers all Annex X raw materials and risk categories
Documented grievance mechanism based on the UN Guiding Principles (early-warning and remediation)
6.2 Management system integration
Structure the internal management system to support the due diligence policy by assigning responsibility to top management and maintaining records for at least 10 years.
Evidence checklist:
Documented assignment of top-management responsibility
Integration into existing management system (quality, environmental, social)
Record retention procedure covering at least 10 years
Evidence of resources allocated to due diligence
6.3 Risk identification & assessment
Identify and assess the risk of adverse impacts in the supply chain associated with the risk categories in point 2 of Annex X.
Evidence checklist:
Documented risk assessment covering all Annex X risk categories
Methodology and criteria used for identification and prioritisation
Records of stakeholder input and public information considered
Risk management plan and monitoring of mitigation measures
6.4 Supplier engagement & chain of custody

Establish and operate a system of controls and transparency regarding the supply chain, including a chain of custody or traceability system identifying upstream actors. Incorporate due diligence requirements into supplier contracts.
Evidence checklist:
Traceability system covering cobalt, graphite, lithium and nickel
Supplier information requests and responses
Contractual clauses incorporating due diligence requirements
Documentation of country of origin, quantities and market transactions
Third-party verification reports of suppliers where available
6.5 Third-party verification readiness
The due diligence policies must be verified by a notified body (Art. 51) and periodically audited. The system must be ready for verification and surveillance.
Evidence checklist:
Readiness for notified body verification covering all Art. 49–50 activities
Previous verification reports and approval decisions (if available)
Access arrangements for audits and surveillance
Evidence of periodic audits by the notified body
6.6 Annual public report

On an annual basis, review and make publicly available a report on the battery due diligence policy, including steps taken, significant adverse impacts and how they were addressed, and a summary of third-party verifications.
Evidence checklist:
Published annual due diligence report
Content covering Art. 52(3) requirements
Process for annual review and publication
Summary of third-party verifications including name of notified body
6.7 Reference to international instruments
The due diligence system must consider the international instruments listed in Annex X points 3 and 4 (UNGPs, OECD Guidelines, ILO conventions, etc.).
Evidence checklist:
Explicit reference to relevant instruments in the policy and procedures
Evidence that risk management measures are consistent with those instruments
Alignment with OECD Due Diligence Guidance and UN Guiding Principles
7. Battery Passport (Article 77, Annex XIII)

From 18 February 2027, each LMT battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and each electric vehicle battery must have an electronic battery passport. The passport is accessible via the QR code and unique identifier and contains public and restricted information as specified in Annex XIII.
7.1 Unique identifier assignment
The economic operator placing the battery on the market shall attribute a unique identifier to it. The QR code and unique identifier must comply with the ISO/IEC 15459 series of standards.
Evidence checklist:
System for assigning unique identifiers compliant with ISO/IEC 15459 series
Records of assigned identifiers linked to individual batteries
Evidence of upload to the EU registry (Art. 77(10))
Process ensuring uniqueness and permanence of identifiers
7.2 Passport data completeness
The battery passport must contain all information required by Annex XIII, differentiated by access rights (public, notified bodies/authorities, persons with legitimate interest).
Evidence checklist:
Complete data set for all applicable Annex XIII points
Separation of public and restricted data fields
Evidence that information is based on open standards and is interoperable
Data authentication, reliability and integrity measures in place
7.3 QR code linkage
The battery passport shall be accessible through the QR code referred to in Article 13(6).
Evidence checklist:
Functional QR code on the battery (or packaging) linking to the passport
Testing records confirming correct linkage and data retrieval
QR code in high contrast and of readable size
7.4 Accuracy and update process
The economic operator shall ensure that the information in the battery passport is accurate, complete and up to date.
Evidence checklist:
Procedure for initial population and ongoing updates of passport data
Defined responsibilities and authorisation for data changes
Records of updates and version control
Process for transferring responsibility in case of re-use, repurposing or remanufacturing
7.5 Registry upload
The unique identifier must be uploaded to the registry referred to in Article 13(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781.
Evidence checklist:
Process and records of successful registry uploads
Confirmation of successful registration for each identifier
Evidence of compliance with registry technical requirements
8. Labelling & QR Code (Article 13, Annex VI)

Article 13 and Annex VI specify the labelling and marking requirements that apply from different dates. All batteries must carry the separate collection symbol from 18 August 2025. General information, capacity and other labels apply from 2026. The QR code becomes mandatory from 18 February 2027.
8.1 Article 13 labelling

Batteries shall bear a label containing the general information set out in Part A of Annex VI. Rechargeable portable, LMT and SLI batteries must also show capacity information. Non-rechargeable portable batteries must show minimum average duration and a 'non-rechargeable' indication.
Evidence checklist:

Labels containing all required general information (Annex VI Part A): manufacturer identification, category, place and date of manufacture, weight, capacity, chemistry, hazardous substances, usable extinguishing agent, critical raw materials >0.1 %
Capacity information where applicable
Chemical symbols (Cd or Pb) correctly placed and sized where required
Separate collection symbol correctly sized and placed
Label printed or engraved visibly, legibly and indelibly (or on packaging/documents where size does not allow)
8.2 QR code presence

From 18 February 2027 all batteries shall be marked with a QR code as described in Part C of Annex VI. The QR code provides access to the battery passport (for relevant categories) or to other required information.
Evidence checklist:
QR code affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly
QR code functional and linking to correct information
Where placement on battery is not possible, correct placement on packaging and documents
QR code in high contrast to the background and of readable size
8.3 Instructions & safety information
Clear, understandable and readable instructions and safety information must accompany the battery in the language(s) required by the Member State.
Evidence checklist:
Instructions covering installation, use, maintenance and disposal
Safety information addressing identified hazards
Availability in all required languages
Evidence that instructions are clear, understandable and readable
9. Performance, Durability, Safety

Articles 6, 9, 10, 12 and 14 establish requirements on hazardous substances, electrochemical performance and durability, safety of stationary battery energy storage systems, and access to battery management system data.
9.1 Hazardous substances restrictions
Article 6 and Annex I restrict the use of mercury, cadmium and lead in batteries. Batteries must not contain these substances above the specified thresholds (with limited exceptions).
Evidence checklist:
Material declarations or test reports confirming compliance with Annex I limits
Supplier certificates for restricted substances
Process controls preventing introduction of restricted substances
Evidence of ongoing monitoring of material composition
9.2 Performance & durability values

Articles 9 and 10 establish minimum values for electrochemical performance and durability parameters. Portable batteries of general use (excluding button cells) must meet the values set out in Annex III from 2028. Similar requirements apply to other categories.
Evidence checklist:
Test reports demonstrating compliance with applicable performance and durability parameters
Documentation of the parameters measured and test conditions used
Evidence that minimum values of the relevant delegated act are met
Test reports from competent laboratories
9.3 Safety of stationary storage (Article 12 + Annex V)

Article 12 requires that stationary battery energy storage systems are safe during normal operation and use. The technical documentation must demonstrate successful testing for the safety parameters set out in Annex V, using state-of-the-art testing methodologies. The parameters apply only in so far as a corresponding hazard exists. An assessment of possible safety hazards not addressed in Annex V must also be included, with evidence that those hazards have been mitigated and tested.
Evidence checklist:
Safety assessment and test reports covering all applicable Annex V parameters at pack/system level
Evidence of safety during normal operation, including thermal and electrical safety
Mitigation measures for identified hazards not covered by Annex V
Residual-risk analysis
Demonstration that testing used state-of-the-art methodologies (primarily IEC 62619:2022 or equivalent)
Clear indication which Annex V parameters are applicable based on residual hazards
9.4 BMS data access

Article 14 requires that up-to-date data for the parameters set out in Annex VII are contained in the battery management system of stationary battery energy storage systems, LMT batteries and electric vehicle batteries, and that read-only access is provided to authorised persons.
Evidence checklist:
BMS functionality providing the Annex VII parameters
Evidence of read-only access provision to authorised users (purchasers, independent operators, waste management operators)
Software reset function available where required
Documentation of data formats and access methods
10. Factory / Module D1 Requirements

When Module D1 is applied, the manufacturer must operate an approved quality system covering production, inspection and testing. The system is subject to initial assessment and ongoing surveillance by the notified body, including on-site audits.
10.1 Quality system documentation
Full quality system documentation covering production, inspection and testing, including quality objectives, organisational structure, processes and records.
Evidence checklist:
Quality manual and supporting procedures
Description of quality objectives and organisational responsibilities
Notified body approval of the quality system
Quality system documentation kept available for 10 years
10.2 Process controls & work instructions
Current work instructions and process control records must be available and followed.
Evidence checklist:
Current work instructions for all critical processes
Process control records demonstrating compliance
Evidence of process capability and control limits
Documented process validation where applicable
10.3 Incoming material & supplier control
Incoming inspection and supplier management records relevant to regulated requirements must be maintained.
Evidence checklist:
Supplier evaluation and approval records
Incoming inspection records for critical materials
Controls related to restricted substances, carbon footprint and recycled content data
Supplier quality agreements
10.4 Inspection & test records
In-process and final product inspection and test records must be maintained.
Evidence checklist:
In-process inspection records
Final product test and inspection records
Calibration records for measuring equipment
Personnel qualification and training records
10.5 Nonconforming product control
Procedure and records for control of nonconforming product and corrective actions must be in place.
Evidence checklist:
Documented nonconforming product control procedure
Records of nonconformities and disposition
Corrective and preventive action records
Analysis of root causes
10.6 Batch traceability
Traceability from batch to materials, design and test results must be maintained.
Evidence checklist:
Traceability records linking finished product to raw materials and components
Ability to retrieve design and test data for any batch
Retention of traceability records for the required period
10.7 Change control
Documented change management for design or production process changes must be in place.
Evidence checklist:
Change control procedure
Records of changes and their impact assessment
Notification to notified body of relevant quality system changes
Verification of continued conformity after changes
10.8 CF / recycled content / DD process controls
Specific records and process controls for carbon footprint data, recycled content and due diligence information must be maintained as part of the quality system.
Evidence checklist:
Procedures for collecting and verifying carbon footprint input data
Controls ensuring accuracy of recycled content calculations
Integration of due diligence information into the quality system
Records demonstrating ongoing monitoring of these data
11. Safety, Performance and Transport Testing

Test reports demonstrating compliance with applicable safety, performance and durability requirements must form part of the technical documentation. For stationary battery energy storage systems, Annex V defines the safety parameters that must be demonstrated. UN 38.3 testing is a transport precondition and is not required by the EU Battery Regulation or by notified bodies for CE marking.
11.1 Annex V safety parameters (SBESS only)

Article 12 and Annex V require that stationary battery energy storage systems are successfully tested for the following safety parameters, using state-of-the-art methodologies. The parameters apply only where a corresponding hazard exists. Testing is required at the complete pack/system level; cell-level certificates provide supporting evidence but do not fully discharge the pack producer’s obligation.
Annex V parameters to be demonstrated:
1. Thermal shock and cycling – evaluates integrity under extreme temperature changes
2. External short-circuit protection – evaluates over-current protection and avoidance of hazardous situations
3. Overcharge protection – evaluates safety under overcharge (voltage or current control)
4. Over-discharge protection – evaluates safety under over-discharge conditions
5. Over-temperature protection – evaluates failure of temperature control
6. Thermal propagation protection – evaluates cascading thermal runaway (key system-level test)
7. Mechanical damage by external forces – evaluates real-life mechanical stresses
8. Internal short circuit – evaluates safety in internal short-circuit situations
9. Thermal abuse – exposure to elevated temperatures (e.g. 85 °C per IEC 62619)
10. Fire test – assessment of explosion risk by exposure to fire
11. Emission of gases – identification of hazardous gas emissions during tests (to be considered for all parameters)
Evidence checklist:
Test reports for all applicable Annex V parameters performed on the complete pack/system
Clear indication of which parameters are applicable based on residual-risk analysis
Evidence that state-of-the-art testing methodologies (primarily IEC 62619:2022 or equivalent) were used
Assessment of possible safety hazards not addressed in Annex V, with evidence of mitigation and testing
Cell-level test certificates retained as supporting evidence where relevant
Sample plan documented and agreed with the test laboratory and notified body
11.2 Sample quantities for Annex V testing

The Regulation does not prescribe fixed sample quantities. Sample numbers are determined by the chosen test methods (primarily IEC 62619:2022). Most functional-safety and product-safety tests on the battery system require a minimum of 1 sample. In practice, laboratories request several full packs.
Evidence checklist / planning guidance:
Documented sample plan based on IEC 62619:2022 (or equivalent state-of-the-art standard)
Theoretical minimum approximately 4–6 packs (several tests can share samples)
Practical number accepted by laboratories and notified bodies: typically 6–12 packs for a full Annex V programme on one pack type
Recommended planning quantity: 8–10 complete packs of the exact type
Specific guidance: Thermal shock usually 1–2 packs; Thermal propagation 1–2 (occasionally 3); Fire test usually 1 pack
Functional-safety tests (overcharge, over-discharge, over-temperature, short-circuit) typically 1 pack each
Confirmation of final sample plan with both the test laboratory and the notified body
11.3 UN 38.3 test summary & reports (transport only)

UN 38.3 testing is required under dangerous-goods transport regulations and is not a requirement of the EU Battery Regulation or of notified bodies for CE marking. A Test Summary must nevertheless be available for transport. Full reports support the Test Summary.
Evidence checklist:
UN 38.3 Test Summary available for transport
Full test reports for applicable tests T.1–T.8 from a competent laboratory
Evidence that testing was performed on representative samples
Clear separation of UN 38.3 documentation from EU Battery Regulation conformity evidence
11.4 Laboratory competence evidence
Evidence that testing was performed by a competent laboratory (ISO/IEC 17025 expectation).
Evidence checklist:
ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation scope covering the relevant tests
Laboratory accreditation certificates and scope documents
Where non-accredited laboratories are used, justification and competence evidence
Evidence of laboratory independence and competence
12. Records & Ongoing Conformity

Manufacturers must maintain records demonstrating that series production remains in conformity, handle conformity-related complaints, and provide full access to documentation and records during notified body audits.
12.1 Ongoing conformity records
Records demonstrating that series production remains in conformity with the Regulation (Art. 38(5)).
Evidence checklist:
Periodic verification or sampling records confirming continued conformity
Records of process monitoring and product testing
Evidence that changes have been assessed for impact on conformity
Surveillance audit reports from the notified body (Module D1)
12.2 Complaint handling related to conformity
Process and records for handling conformity-related complaints.
Evidence checklist:
Documented complaint handling procedure
Records of conformity-related complaints and actions taken
Link to corrective action process

12.3 Access during audits
Readiness to provide full access to documentation and records during notified body audits (Annex VIII + Art. 38).
Evidence checklist:
Organised and retrievable documentation system
Designated personnel available to support audits
Access rights and procedures for external auditors
Ability to provide documentation in electronic format (and paper on request)
End of Checklist
